idea: Week two, from the story bank: written from the tables, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: Gujarat's share of India's pulses production rose from 3.34% (574.5 of 17,191.3 thousand tonnes) in 2014-15 to 7.87% (2,022.1 of 25,682.5) in 2024-25, with the harvest 3.5 times bigger against India's 1.5 times, on 2.2 times the area and 1.6 times the yield, and 17% of India's extra pulses.

Lower share can mean more tonnes. State totals, not per person. Blank: Jammu and Kashmir (boundary changed); Delhi (no output in 2014-15); Ladakh and four small UTs (not in table). The table shows how much, not why.
source: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, as published in the RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 61: production of pulses, thousand tonnes, shown here in lakh tonnes. Each share is of the all-India figure in the same table. Area is Table 70 and yield is Table 83. The 2024-25 column is the Ministry's final estimate. Left blank on the map: Jammu and Kashmir (boundary changed in 2019); Delhi (no pulses output in 2014-15); not in the table: Ladakh, Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
